focus: The DESIGN.md question: spec schema, location, consumption path, safe defaults, and rubric integration; consolidation of per-type divergence
noveltyJustification: New ground: external DESIGN.md/DTCG conventions, the spec consumption path through compose_board.py, the three-way palette split, and the mirror's resolved-constants strategy; finding 9 deepens iteration 1 finding 15.
keyQuestions: What does the sk-create-figjam composer's design surface control today — palette, type scale, grid, zones, shapes, connectors, key, title block and source line — and where is each value set in compose-board.js and the packet references?

How well do the nine rendered boards in assets/screenshots hold up as visual design — first-glance hierarchy, alignment and spacing rhythm, type scale and weight, colour harmony and contrast, connector routing and label legibility, zone tints, the key, and density?
Where do the seven diagram types diverge in colour, zones and layout, which divergences are deliberate per-type identity and which are inconsistencies to unify?

Should the packet read a user-editable design spec file in the spirit of a DESIGN.md Style Reference, and if so where would it live, what schema would it carry, how would compose_board.py, the composer and the claude.ai Project mirror read it, and how would validation keep bad edits safe?
What do the current boards already do well that must be preserved, and how should the quality rubric and board scorecard check a board against a design spec?

ruledOut: Raw DTCG JSON as the spec envelope — it is tool-interchange format; markdown+YAML is the hand-editable layer the question asks for
Repository-root DESIGN.md as the spec's only location — it collides with sk-design's artifact name and overreaches scope
Spec-file parametrisation of the routing solver, layout algorithm, key membership, or spacing bands
Refusing to compose on a malformed spec — style degrades gracefully to defaults; only model errors refuse

label: Google's DESIGN.md convention is the borrowable precedent: YAML front-matter/interleaved token blocks (normative) + markdown rationale; 'design counterpart to AGENTS.md'; published as @google/design.md (~208k weekly downloads)

W3C DTCG Format Module reached first stable version 2025.10: typed tokens via $type, named groups, {path} aliases, theming — borrow typed groups + aliases inside a markdown/YAML envelope, not raw DTCG JSON

sk-design-md-generator's v3 rules translate directly: verbatim values from one token source, named semantic roles, validator checking hex accuracy + section completeness — the packet's composer constants are already the measured baseline
The md-generator refuses forward-authoring (measured-only boundary); a board spec is authored defaults — the packet owns a hand-authored spec seeded verbatim from current constants, not an extraction

Consumption path exists: compose_board.py substitutes __MODEL__ into the template under the 50k use_figma ceiling — a spec rides as a second injected constants block (e.g. __STYLE__), zero extra calls

Palette truth is split three ways today (composer constants, ACCENT_PAIRS in figjam_checks/common.py, the mirrored knowledge copy); the spec becomes the source the first two are validated against; the mirror ships resolved constants

The self-test already regex-parses compose-board.js as a de facto spec (SHAPE_PAIR/KIND_PAIR → accent hue >=45deg, mark gate >=3:1); a declared spec file replaces fragile source parsing with a normative token surface
Validation machinery is already owned: contrast(), hue_of(), MIN_HUE_APART=45, 4.5:1 text and 3.0:1 mark gates — spec validation re-runs them on user-edited tokens

Per-type divergence is kind vocabulary not style (deepens iter-1 f15): sequence colours by arrow kind + numbered pins and takes no zones; state colours by role with composites as zones — the spec surface is shared per-kind tokens, not per-type themes

Safe defaults follow packet philosophy (model errors refuse, style degrades): every key optional→current constant; unparseable file→warn+full fallback; floor-failing token→rejected to default, never fails the board

Spec location: packet level (file under sk-create-figjam/), not repo root (name collision with sk-design's DESIGN.md + scope overreach); optional user override discovered by walking up from the model file; mirror gets a knowledge copy via SYNC.md
Rubric integration is a wording change: Section 7 'Colour by meaning' and 'Key and source' score against the loaded spec's kind table instead of the hardcoded one; scorecard semantics survive
Hard boundary on non-token concerns: routing solver costs, layout algorithm, key membership and judgment bands stay out of the spec — exposing them breaks invariants a user cannot see
Deciding trade-off: non-native spec colours silently break FigJam picker recolouring — spec keys colours by semantic pair and warns on non-native values, paying that cost explicitly for user theming

Spec schema: colors.pairs/colors.kinds, accent{pair,nodeWeight8,messageWeight4}, zones{tints,cycle,labelType}, type{family,ramp}, spacing{grid8,cross80,rank136,zone48/96/48,board80,key64}, shapes kind→shape+radius, connectors{color,weight2,dash,caps,label}, key/title/subtitle/source furniture — all optional, defaults = current constants
